issues.description: The Problem Statement defines ExcellenceLand.excellentEnough as a boolean and requires public getters for all attributes. In the Solution, the getter isExcellentEnough() returns a String ("yes"/"no") instead of a boolean. This is a structural return-type mismatch for the getter: tests or student implementations will expect a boolean-returning getter for a boolean attribute and will be unable to rely on the declared attribute type. This will cause confusion and failures in automated checks that expect a boolean getter signature (e.g., public boolean isExcellentEnough()).
issues.suggested_fix: Change the getter to return a boolean consistent with the attribute type. For example, implement public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; } (or public boolean getExcellentEnough()), and avoid converting the boolean to a String. Ensure the constructor and getter names/signatures match the exercise's expectations so automated tests and students' implementations align with the UML specification.
